12. On the other hand Mr. A. J. Mohammad Ali, learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the respondent nos.1(a)- 1(h), 2-3 submits that the deed dated 09.06.1917 executed by Md. Azim Mollah and Md. Abdul Mollah infavour of Asmat Ullah and Jasmat Ullah was a conditional sale and the condition not being complied with, it was not acted upon and accordingly C.S. Khalian was prepared in the name of original owners but the trial court erroneously shifted the onus upon the plaintiffs as such the impugned judgment and decree shall sustain. He also submits that C.S. Khatian has presumption of its correctness which is suit rebatable by proper evidence but no evidence was adduced by the contesting defendants to discharge their onus which lawfully lies on them and the trial court failed to appreciate the evidence adduced by the plaintiffs and thus erroneously holding title and possession of the defendants. He again submits that Khatian has no presumptive value as such the impugned judgment and decree shall sustain and the appeal is liable to be dismissed. He lastly submits that the plaintiffs categorically stated in the plaint that: 

 "Considering the evidence adduced by the defendant-respondents it does not appear that the consideration money for the deed dated 09.06.1917 i.e. exhibit 'Ica' was paid to the ex-landlord. It appears that trial court courageously fixed the onus of such proof on the plaintiff-appellants. The rebuttal onus always lies with the other side who wants to repudiates the presumption as the C.S. record of rights hold. 

 22. As per provisions of Section 90 of the Evidence Act there is a presumption infavour of a thirty years old original copy of a registered deed which is submitted in the court from proper custody. For proper appreciation Section 90 of the Evidence Act is reproduced below: 

 "90. Presumption as to documents thirty years old: Where any document, purporting or proved to be thirty years old, is produced from any custody which the Court in the particular case considers proper, the Court may presume that the signature and every other part of such document, which purports to be in the handwriting of any particular person, is in that person's handwriting, and, in the case of a document executed or attested, that it was duly executed and attested by the persons by whom it purports to be executed and attested. 

 23. From the provisions of above mentioned Section of the Evidence Act it appears that the exhibited copy of thirty years old registered document dated 05.01.1923 is being an original copy and produced before the court from proper custody as such the presumption infavour of deed no.112 dated 05.01.1923 is that the said deed is a genuine one. In such a situation the onus of proof of the allegation of the plaintiffs regarding lending money by taking signature in blank stamp and thereafter used the same to create forged document by the predecessor of the defendant nos.67 and 68 lies upon the plaintiffs.
